findings.text: The premise assumes `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` always stores integers, but [WITHOUT ROWID tables](https://www.sqlite.org/withoutrowid.html#differences_from_ordinary_rowid_tables) permit text: `customers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY COLLATE BINARY) WITHOUT ROWID` containing `'a'` and `blocked(customer_id TEXT NOT NULL COLLATE NOCASE)` containing `'A'` satisfy the stated premises while `NOT IN` returns `'a'` and `NOT EXISTS` returns nothing. Fix: require `customers.id` to be an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY that aliases the rowid.
